title: Insulin: structure, secretion and signalling
sec: Insulin: structure, secretion and signalling · p927
guide: Insulin has 51 amino acids in A and B chains with disulphide bonds; the precursor is preproinsulin; receptor is a tyrosine kinase signalling via IRS. Glucose is the most potent stimulus; first and second phases of secretion reflect stored and newly made insulin.

title: GLUT transporters, C-peptide and incretin physiology
sec: GLUT transporters, C-peptide and incretin physiology · p928
guide: GLUT1/3/4 differ in tissue specificity; GLUT2 is the β-cell glucose sensor; GLUT4 is insulin-stimulated. C-peptide tracks endogenous insulin and helps separate insulinoma / sulfonylurea use from exogenous insulin. GLP-1 and GIP are incretins with different half-lives.

title: Incretin therapies and dual agonists
sec: Incretin therapies and dual agonists · p929
guide: GLP-1 agonists (exenatide, liraglutide, semaglutide) and the dual GLP-1/GIP agonist tirzepatide reduce HbA1c with weight loss and cardiovascular benefit. Caution for pancreatitis and medullary thyroid disease.

title: DKA: pathophysiology, features, investigations
guide: DKA arises from insulin deficiency with glucagon excess driving lipolysis and ketogenesis. Triggers include infection, MI, missed insulin, pregnancy and cocaine. β-hydroxybutyrate predominates; urine dipstick detects acetoacetate.

title: DKA management, HHS, overlap
guide: DKA fluids start with 0.9% saline, regular insulin 0.1 U/kg bolus then 0.1 U/kg/h; add KCl once K+ <5.2 and dextrose when glucose <200 mg/dL. HHS has 12 L deficit, glucose >600 mg/dL and worse prognosis. SGLT2 inhibitors cause euglycaemic DKA.

title: Insulin regimens, dawn/Somogyi, CGM
guide: Basal-bolus, premixed, CSII and twice-daily NPH are the main regimens. Distinguish dawn phenomenon from Somogyi by checking 3 a.m. glucose. CGM reduces hypoglycaemia and provides TIR, variability and GMI metrics.
